title: Stone Game
statement:
Alice and Bob play a game with piles of stones. There are an even number of piles arranged in a row, and each pile has a positive integer number of stones.
Alice and Bob take turns, with Alice going first. Each turn, a player takes the entire pile of stones from either the beginning or the end of the row.
The player with the most stones at the end wins.
Both players play optimally. Return `YES` if Alice wins the game, or `NO` if Bob wins.
inputFormat:
Line 1: an integer N.
Line 2: N space-separated integers.

examples.explanation: Alice wins regardless of Bob's moves.
Alice picks 3 (left), Bob picks 7, Alice picks 3 (right), Bob picks 2. Alice=6>Bob=9... actually Alice goes first and wins optimally.

starterCode.python:
n = int(input())
piles = list(map(int, input().split()))
